chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If harshness (al-khuruq) were a visible creature, there would not be anything among what Allah created uglier than it.'

key_terms.الْخُرْقُ: Harshness, coarseness, or awkwardness of manners/character

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean when he says harshness is the ugliest creation?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that 'al-khuruq' represents a profound defect in one's spiritual constitution, not merely a social faux pas. By personifying harsh manners as a visible creature, the Prophet (PBUH) illustrates its visceral repulsiveness, aligning with the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a mirror of inner faith. This teaching serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate gentleness, contrasting the 'ugliness' of coarse behavior with the beauty of noble character.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from ali Bin Al Numan, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
that ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Had the harshness being a visible creature, there would not have been anything from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Created, uglier than it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Had harshness been among the visible creatures it would have looked the most loathsome of the creatures of Allah.’”
